claims.claim: The company delivered a 31 percent increase in PRASK, exceeding the guidance of more than 25 percent growth.
claims.quote: we delivered a 31 percent increase in PRASK, which exceeded our guidance of more than 25 percent growth.

claims.claim: The benchmark Singapore jet fuel index was 60 percent higher than Q2 last year, leading to a 69 percent increase in fuel CASK.
claims.quote: The benchmark Singapore jet fuel index was 60 percent higher than Q2 last year. This increase, along with the rupee depreciation, flowed directly through to our cost base, a 69 percent increase in our fuel CASK.

claims.claim: The company reported a net loss of 19 billion rupees for the quarter ended September 30, 2026.
claims.quote: For the quarter ended 30 September 2026, we reported a net loss of 19 billion rupees

claims.claim: The company ended the quarter with total cash of 527 billion rupees.
claims.quote: we continue to maintain a strong liquidity position, ending the quarter with total cash of 527 billion rupees

claims.claim: Passenger demand held up as we served 31.3 million passengers, a growth of ~1% year over year.
claims.quote: Despite a volatile environment, passenger demand held up as we served 31.3 million passengers, a growth of ~1% year over year.

claims.claim: The quarter was marked by constructive pricing environment, and our ability to pass through a part of the elevated fuel and operating-cost pressure.
claims.quote: The quarter was marked by constructive pricing environment, and our ability to pass through a part of the elevated fuel and operating-cost pressure in a disciplined manner.

claims.claim: EBITDAR came in at 38.3 billion rupees at a margin of 15.6% compared to 28% for the same period last year.
claims.quote: In terms of profitability, EBITDAR came in at 38.3 billion rupees at a margin of 15.6% compared to an EBITDAR of 57.4 billion rupees and a margin of 28% for the same period last year.

claims.claim: Demand is currently inelastic to fare hikes.
claims.quote: For the moment, what we are seeing is as we take the fares up, the market is inelastic to these hikes in fares.

claims.claim: Domestic fuel cost increases have been largely passed through.
claims.quote: On the domestic side, we have managed to recover to a large part, the increased cost that is there

claims.claim: The company maintains a liquidity safety net of 20-25% of annual revenue.
claims.quote: it's always prudent to keep at least 20% to 25% of your overall top line as a safety net.

claims.claim: IndiGo was the largest recipient of Airbus aircraft globally for the second consecutive year.
claims.quote: An important milestone is our position as the largest recipient of Airbus aircraft globally for the second consecutive year, accounting for around 7% of all Airbus deliveries worldwide.

claims.claim: The company served 124 million customers in calendar year 2025, a 9% increase year-over-year.
claims.quote: For the full calendar year 2025, we had the privilege of serving around 124 million or 12.4 crore customers, a 9 percent increase on a year over year basis.

claims.claim: Fuel CASK reduced by 3% despite a 2% increase in benchmark Singapore Jet fuel prices.
claims.quote: our fuel CASK has reduced by 3 percent compared to an increase of around 2 percent in benchmark Singapore Jet fuel prices

claims.claim: The company has a total of 28 owned aircraft at the quarter end.
claims.quote: With this transaction we have a total of 28 owned aircraft at the quarter end and around 20% of aircraft either owned or finance leased.

claims.claim: The company reported a profit of 1 billion rupees excluding foreign exchange and hedging impacts.
claims.quote: we reported a profit of 1 billion rupees or 104 crore rupees against a loss of INR 7.5 billion rupees, during the same period last year.

claims.claim: The company has a net foreign exchange exposure of approximately 9 billion dollars.
claims.quote: the net exposure as of the end of September is approximately 9 billion dollars.

claims.claim: The company aims to have 30-40% of its fleet on the balance sheet by 2030.
claims.quote: By 2030, our goal is to have 30 – 40% of our total fleet held on our balance sheet either in the form of owned or finance leased structures.

claims.claim: Fuel CASK reduced by 16% year-over-year due to lower fuel prices and redelivery of older damp-leased aircraft.
claims.quote: the fuel CASK reduced by around 16 percent on a year over year basis largely driven by reduction in fuel prices and the redelivery of some older-generation damp leased aircraft.

claims.claim: While the industry passengers grew by around 6 percent, we served more than 31 million customers, reflecting a solid growth of 12 percent.
claims.quote: while the industry passengers grew by around 6 percent, we served more than 31 million customers, reflecting a solid growth of 12 percent compared to the same period last year.

claims.claim: Profitability was impacted by ongoing geopolitical headwinds, this was partially offset by a favorable fuel price environment.
claims.quote: While profitability was impacted by ongoing geopolitical headwinds, this was partially offset by a favorable fuel price environment.

claims.claim: Fuel CASK reduced by 21.9 percent on a year over year basis driven by a reduction in average fuel prices, contract negotiation and redeliveries of older generation aircraft.
claims.quote: the fuel CASK reduced by 21.9 percent on a year over year basis driven by a reduction in average fuel prices, contract negotiation and redeliveries of older generation aircraft

Is there a rethink on the fleet strategy for the year given the flattish capacity growth?
Will pricing be determined by costs or demand disruption?
Why did employee costs fall sequentially despite hiring?
What is the actual shortage of pilots to run full capacity?
Are there recurring impacts on CASK ex-fuel from the cancellation episode?
Is the optimistic capacity addition based on data or just capturing market share?
What kind of savings can we expect from the new captive MRO unit?
Is the mid to high single digit ASK growth a reflection of expected slowdown continuing?
What is happening with the increased aircraft incidents in recent months at IndiGo?

synthesis.one_liner: IndiGo exhibits accelerating top-line growth and positive cash conversion, countered by heavy losses, compressed operating margins, and severe balance sheet leverage.

narrative_vs_numbers.says: Passenger demand remains resilient and capacity additions continue across quarters.
narrative_vs_numbers.shows: Trailing twelve-month revenue reached ₹93,858 cr (+13%), with quarterly growth accelerating to +26% YoY in Sep 2026.

narrative_vs_numbers.says: Constructive pricing environments allow pass-through of fuel and operating-cost pressures.
narrative_vs_numbers.shows: Trailing PAT dropped to −₹4,105 cr, down −180%, with a quarterly loss of −₹1,879 cr despite an 8.2% operating margin.

narrative_vs_numbers.says: Liquidity safety nets are actively maintained to buffer against operational shocks.
narrative_vs_numbers.shows: Borrowings stand at ₹87,303 cr against equity of ₹4,996 cr, yielding a debt-to-equity ratio of 17.47x.

narrative_vs_numbers.says: Operations generate substantial scale and customer volume across domestic routes.
narrative_vs_numbers.shows: Cumulative free cash flow reached ₹78,358 cr over 5 years, with the latest annual free cash flow at ₹21,767 cr.

synthesis.credibility: Management guidance lacks verifiable ledger outcomes due to non-comparable headline reporting, showing zero measured hits or misses across 22 tracked items while shifting capacity targets downward.

bull.evidence: Revenue has compounded at 42% over 5 years and 16% over 3 years.
Free cash flow was positive in all of the last 5 years, totaling ₹78,358 cr.
Operating cash conversion reached 156% over 5 years, yielding ₹83,658 cr.

bear.evidence: Borrowings of ₹87,303 cr against equity of ₹4,996 cr drive debt to equity to 17.47x.
Trailing-twelve-month PAT fell to −₹4,105 cr, representing a −180% decline.

bear.point: Heavy debt burden relative to earnings
bear.evidence: Gross debt is 7.7x trailing operating profit, exceeding three years of EBITDA.

watch: Check whether quarterly operating margin sustains above the 8.2% reported in Sep 2026.
Monitor debt-to-equity trajectory from the current 17.47x level.
